reviews.review: Game has a ton of potential. All of the bones needed for a fun game are there, the rest are details. I look forward to exploring the beautiful environments and I'm sure once more features get added like the Season pass it's going to be a blast.

It's a solid LFD style experience with a sci-fi aesthetic. At present, the EA launch is very bare bones and light on content, though I think they have a strong foundation if they can add more content and refine the core gameplay loop.

I don't like horror, and I don't like zombies--this game is a great way for me to enjoy the horde-shooter genre. The groovy style and bright colors break the mold and are a breath of fresh air. I hope more games follow this trend so there are more options for people who want something outside of the grungy-realistic feel of most shooters.

Its like an already better version of Back 4 Blood.
Sure, its Early Access(E.A.) but this game has a lot of character. Really enjoy the random perk generator.
This game shows a lot of promise and I'm excited to have it in my Library.

It runs better than Back4Blood which is a horrible game. No a reddit AMA will not make this dev. The devs of Evolve a good one. No playing a game for 300h to get the right cards will not make the game suddenly rewarding.

About Anacrusis. This is a generic "no starwars, no alien franchise game á la DeathLoop with even less character than DL (PS: I think I mean Dying Light)."
People do not seem to play this. Guns are god awful. Look at the trailers on steam. Soulless Unity trash in UE4.
HDR is fun and does not work cause Windows 10. Rooms are empty but sharply rendered. If this is early access then this game is pre-alpha just for the boredom of walking through snake levels from the get-go.

DO NO BUY FOR THE LOVE OF YOUR WALLET AND TO VOTE FOR GAMES WITH SOUL.

Unfortunately this game never really took off, which I personally think is largely a branding issue. The game's character ultimately falls flat for players such as myself. From the cover art, the name, the color scheme, the ingame environments, and general design...it never REALLY pulled me into it. This could be my own bias but I've always actually really disliked space settings and find them very limiting (ironic), forgettable, and just not relatable. I can understand an indie title having very little advertising, but the branding really needs to be spot on.

I do still believe they've got some interesting ideas in this game from a gameplay standpoint, but as a online coop game it needs a larger playerbase to keep people coming back (which the branding isn't doing them any favors here). There is still a considerable lack of content for the base game in regards to the amount of campaigns especially considering it is now out of early access.

My understanding is the company has undergone some financial issues, and I do think that somewhat shows regarding the development of this game. However, some of the decisions were a bit confusing to watch from afar. Having mod support, and adding Versus mode so early on felt like unnecessary things to really work towards. These are *great* additions to have to your game *if* you have the playerbase that will benefit from it, but this game does not.

Ultimately the game fell flat in the time where it should have shown and proven it's potential.

I hate to say it, as a fan of Back 4 Blood and an old retired vet from l4d's gb tourny days, this game is ticking all the old nostalgic feelings that I haven't felt since I waited in line at gamestop for the midnight release of l4d2. This is more fun than b4b, but at the moment needs a lot of growth to fit into its own shoes. There's lots of things coming to this game that are needed but requires player feedback and suggestions to get right. They released the game in early access to have this player input available and help shape the game to become a potential masterpiece. I'm excited to help be a part of this games growth and help foster a new community of players with amazing potential!
It is already really fun. If the right features will be added until the end of early access, this has potential to be awesome!
Fun and challenging, The style is a nice change of pace from the standard zombie shooter

very similar to left 4 dead this early on in development, which is a good sign. the enemies are easily identifiable, there are plenty of grenades and weapons, upgrades to unlock throughout the maps, big hordes, tense fights, great music, funny moments, the list goes on. the anacrusis doesn't make any drastic changes to the formula we're familiar with, unlike back 4 blood. it's pretty much more of the same fun l4d gameplay you're used to, with its own unique twists. if you're a fan of l4d, definitely give this game a try as it should only get better as development continues

Loved it.
I have really high hopes for this game! We had a lot of fun playing it and it works amazing for an early access. The style it's vivid and colorful, the weapons are reeeeeally cool and the vortex bomb it's really fun to watch!

It does have some bugs (nothing mayor) but the devs are putting a lot of love into this game, so I'm sure they'll get fixed pretty soon.

I have really high hopes for this game! Totally worth it!

This is definitely the kind of experience I was looking for when I tried B4B. New enemy mechanics, new weapons, fun gameplay. This game is not perfect, there's bugs here and there and sometimes levels can prove a bit difficult, but with friends and good communication skills, you can definitely have a blast! I will be looking forward for future updates!
Still relatively early in development, but what they have right now is incredibly solid. Very excited to see where future content updates go!

I played acts 1 and 2 while the game is in beta.release from Jan 13th. I expected a space shooter with funk themes and I got a space shooter with funk themes. 

Firstly, and so that people come in with the correct expectation, this is still in beta and not a full release game. With that being said the Anacrusis supplies a 4 person coop shooter that matches the same itch the campaigns in the Left 4 Dead series.

I will update this review once I finish the act/more content gets released. To note, I have replayed act 1 and 2 a few times and was pleasantly surprised the AI director does alternate paths as well as change the location of perks/special weapon spawns. It takes the positive game play that was in left 3 dead and applies them here.

Funny that an early access game that doesn't advertise being "From the creators of Left 4 Dead" has more life and promise out of it than Back 4 Blood does in its final state.

Only downfall is that there is a set difficulty which seems rather easy, but with it's own difficult points in the game. Can't wait for more content!

So, I'm a huge fan of co-op shooters. I've played a lot of Payday 2, Killing Floor 2, L4D2 and I've been playing Deep Rock recently and dabbled in B4B, mediocre at best that game is. 

The Anacrusis just has this flare that I absolutely love. I'm a sucker for 70's aesthetics, and The Anacrusis nails that to a tee, from the music to the level design, architecture and atmosphere. There are some problems, I will go over those in a bit. But for a foundation, this is one of the best co-op shooters I've played in a while.

Let's start with problems. I've played through all 4 chapters, but have the most experience with Chapter 1. A lot of these are crossed off because these devs are really good at taking in community feedback, which is actually bonkers how much they listen, it's wonderful.

[strike] 1. No text chat/voice chat off by default. This is a very highly team focused game. It's really frustrating when I want to communicate to my team through voice but they don't have it on due to it being off by default. [/strike] Already addressed with a prompt coming to suggest adjusting voice settings on start-up.

[strike] 2. Mouse Acceleration? Question mark because this one doesn't bother me, but it might others, as it has been cited as an issue. [/strike] Addressed and dealt with.

[strike]3. No vote/kick function. I've already been dealing with "teammates" keeping saferooms open so we cannot progress and deliberate friendly fire. My only option is to leave these games, due to no vote option.[/strike] Just fixed with the free weekend!

[strike] 4. Very janky/rapid movement in general. I don't know if this is an engine issue or just early access crust (no offense of course), but when dealing with Brutes, the distance that people are flung and what direction they are flung can vary wildly. It's often disorienting getting hit by a Brute and then teleporting to where you end up. [/strike] Gameplay is a lot more smooth, along with not teleporting places! Thank you devs!

5. Uneven level length. Chapter 1 is objectively the largest of the 3 chapters, and feels like a full L4D "campaign" to me, but the other two chapters, while fun in their own right, don't stack up. Chapter 3 was somewhat close, but Chapter 2 was incredibly short. Just a nitpick/odd design choice I noticed. I'd also like to see the amount of chapters a chapter/campaign has before going into it.

[strike] 6. HUD/Viewmodel bugs. My partner and I ran into a few of these during our playthroughs, and while some could be fixed by just swapping to AFK, others required you to leave the lobby to reset it. This is expected of Early Access, so I'm not too worried about it. [/strike] Already addressed and fixed!

[strike]7. Little weapon variety. 3 primary guns, 1 secondary, and 3 power weapons. The Blaster Rifle feels very lackluster compared to the SMB and Shotgun Blaster. I hope there are more weapons coming before or during post launch.[/strike] Already addressed and have added variants, mods and new weapons as well.

Now, that seems like a lot of negatives that I've come up with, but to me, the positives heavily outweigh them and these negatives can (and have) easily gone away with time.

Here are the positives.

1. Character interaction. I absolutely love when characters interact with one another, and tell a story through their dialogue. I'm getting a lot of vibes from this game from that as well. I'd love even more character interaction between the group! [strike] Side note, I would LOVE a character preference system in this game so you could choose a character preferred that you would want to play as in game, or how you prefer them 1-4, one being most preferred and 4 being least. [/strike] Already addressed and added! These devs listen so much, and it's delightful.

2. The Perk System. This is a fantastic idea to add a huge amount of replayability to this kind of game. A small nitpick i have is some perks are SOOOOO much better than others, (Looking at you Goo Nullifier/Charge Extender/Fast Healing.) and the perk pool is kinda small with 40 at the time of this review. But other than those small gripes, absolutely fantastic. It combines growing power with rewarding exploration, peak game design. This also kinda is a reason I prefer Chapter 1, because of how much I'm able to build my power over the longer course of that mission.

3a. Addictive gameplay and great gunplay. Guns are fun to use, enemies are fun to shoot, what more could you ask for? Another thing this game has going for it is the variety of grenades. There are so many grenades, all of them having really unique purposes, which I really love.

3b. HOLY MOTHER OF MODS, the mod system for guns is actually genius. There's actually a purpose to check guns outside of safe rooms as they could possibly have fantastic mods to help with how you play. I can't believe I didn't think of this sooner, as it's a phenomenal change to the game.

4. Groovy soundtrack/score. More of this please, I love the funky 70s vibe that these jams give off during gameplay, along with how they contribute to the hectic nature of the hordes.

5. AFK mode is wonderful, glad that was salvaged from L4D2. Needs to be normalized in Co-Op shooters. [strike]Slight nitpick, similar to L4D, it would be awesome if it automatically switched on after a certain period of time.[/strike] Fixed, works perfectly now.

6. Specials are unique, easily distinguishable from a crowd, and provide their own unique problems to each fight. Eggs are also super terrifying balls of death that I dread triggering.

7. Crescendo events are nice and varied with different holdout locations or gauntlets. [strike]More crescendos in my opinion need to be specified, however. An example is the run to the saferoom through the park in Chapter 1. Maybe a gate or indicator that it will alert the aliens? Just spitballing.[/strike] Game Instructor is more informative now as well on crescendos!

8. The overall feel and care put into this game. I know you guys are hard at work in this game, and as a message to the devs personally. I am loving this game, this game has a wonderful soul, and I will be watching this game with keen interest for the rest of the year.

So, you could probably tell my feelings overall on this game. This is basically all my thoughts I could sum up in my head at the moment, but as co-op shooters go, this one has the potential of being one of the greats. Pick this one up and give it a shot if you like co-op shooting games. Just expect some EA jank.

Edit: Fixed some things and crossed off negatives that have been addressed/fixed.

Edit 2: This game is getting so much love put into it, I hate seeing so many of the top reviews being negative. It's like I'm taking crazy pills, they're putting so much effort into it with all these patches and changes lifted straight from the community.

Edit 3: Striked out some more fixes that the devs made. Please ignore the top review, he only has less than an hour of playtime and played it when the game came out, this game has gotten significantly better and will only get better with time. At the time of writing this edit, the game is 9 bucks, which is an absolute steal seeing as you get all future battlepasses for free with the game.
